mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which positively impacts consumer confidence and spending, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is low but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production (INDPRO) signals economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth is accompanied by negative S&P 500 returns in more than 50% of cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate increased demand in the housing market, boosting related sectors and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 35% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates tight monetary policy, potentially slowing economic growth and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 45% of cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When both unemployment (UNRATE) is low and payroll employment (PAYEMS) is high, it indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE is low and PAYEMS is high but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 grows but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 35% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When CPI (CPIAUCSL) increases and FEDFUNDS is high, inflationary pressures combined with tight monetary policy may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
regime_hint: inflationary pressures with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If both CPI increases and FEDFUNDS is high but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis fails.
